Messages.Author: oaflord
Messages.Body:
2 quick questions before Autarkis Persecution 2001 in Toronto tomorrow...
hopefully in time...

1. Meth A has a Master Discipline card from Meth B's library left over from
a previous game thus making his deck illegal (whether it be over 90 cards or
different from registration). What course of action should occur, and if
the Meth is removed from the current round does his predator get anything
for it?

2. Meth A and Meth B are friends and sit crosstable from each other at a 4
player table, and Meth C and D do not know each other. How far can Meth A &
B go in helping each other out before it is considered collusion, and if
Meth A & B are privy to each others decks pre-tourney, is that considered
collusion?

Thanks in advance,

oAFLORD

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
oaflord wrote:
>
> 2 quick questions before Autarkis Persecution 2001 in Toronto tomorrow...
> hopefully in time...
>
> 1. Meth A has a Master Discipline card from Meth B's library left over from
> a previous game thus making his deck illegal (whether it be over 90 cards or
> different from registration). What course of action should occur, and if
> the Meth is removed from the current round does his predator get anything
> for it?

Game loss [103]. Allocation of resources (VP, pool for the predator) is up to
the judge and should be based on the table information at the time.

>
> 2. Meth A and Meth B are friends and sit crosstable from each other at a 4
> player table, and Meth C and D do not know each other. How far can Meth A &
> B go in helping each other out before it is considered collusion, and if
> Meth A & B are privy to each others decks pre-tourney, is that considered
> collusion?

They can all go as far as they like.
Collusion involves helping someone else while not helping yourself.
I can't see how.
